title: AgentLens: Revealing The Lucky Pass Problem in SWE-Agent Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2605.12925v5 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Evaluation of software engineering (SWE) agents is dominated by a binary signal: whether the final patch passes the tests. This outcome-only view treats a principled solution and a chaotic trial-and-error process as equivalent. We show that this equivalence is empirically false. We evaluate 2,614 OpenHands trajectories from eight model backends on 60 SWE-bench Verified tasks. Of these, 47 have enough passing trajectories to construct task-level process references, yielding a 1,815-trajectory evaluation subset. Among passing trajectories in this subset, 10.7% exhibit behavior we call a Lucky Pass: regression cycles, blind retries, missing verification, or temporally disordered exploration, implementation, and verification. We introduce AgentLens, a framework for process-level assessment of SWE-agent trajectories, and release AgentLens-Bench, a dataset of 1,815 trajectories annotated with quality scores, waste signals, divergence

translated_title: AgentLens：揭示软件工程智能体评估中的“幸运通过”问题
translated_abstract: 软件工程（SWE）智能体的评估主要受一个二元信号主导：最终补丁是否通过测试。这种仅看结果的观点将有原则的解决方案与混乱的试错过程视为等同。我们证明这种等同性在经验上是错误的。我们在60个SWE-bench Verified任务上评估了来自八个模型后端的2,614条OpenHands轨迹。其中47个任务拥有足够多的通过轨迹来构建任务级的过程参考，从而得到一个包含1,815条轨迹的评估子集。在该子集的通过轨迹中，有10.7%表现出我们称之为“幸运通过”的行为：回归循环、盲目重试、缺失验证，或者探索、实现与验证在时间顺序上的混乱。我们提出了AgentLens，一个用于SWE智能体轨迹过程级评估的框架，并发布了AgentLens-Bench数据集，其中包含1,815条标注了质量分数、浪费信号和分歧信息的轨迹。
tldr: 本文提出AgentLens过程级评估框架并发布AgentLens-Bench数据集，发现10.7%通过测试的智能体轨迹存在“幸运通过”问题（如回归循环、盲目重试、缺失验证等），证明仅以测试是否通过来评估软件工程智能体是不充分的。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AgentLens, a process-level evaluation framework, and the AgentLens-Bench dataset, revealing that 10.7% of passing SWE-agent trajectories exhibit "Lucky Pass" behaviors such as regression cycles, blind retries, and missing verification, demonstrating that outcome-only evaluation is empirically inadequate.
